title: Product sync, 14 March
text:
Product sync, 14 March 2025. Attendees: Dana, Luis, Priya and Wen.

Dana opened with the Q1 numbers: weekly active users reached 48,200, up 12 percent from February. Luis reported that the new onboarding flow cut sign-up drop-off from 31 percent to 19 percent, and recommended keeping it for all new accounts.

The team decided to delay the Android release from 2 April to 16 April because the payment screen still crashes on older devices. Priya owns the fix and will report back on 21 March.

Wen raised the support backlog: 134 open tickets, most about password resets. Action: Wen drafts a self-service reset page by 28 March. The next sync is on 28 March at 10:00.

title: River Esk bridge reopens
text:
The Harcombe Bridge over the River Esk reopened to traffic on Monday after eleven weeks of repairs. Floods in December had undermined two of its piers, and engineers from the county council spent the winter underpinning them with steel piles.

Councillor Janet Moorfield said the work cost 3.4 million pounds, roughly 400,000 pounds over the first estimate because the riverbed was softer than surveys suggested. Buses on the number 14 route resume their normal path from Tuesday, ending a nine-kilometre detour.

The bridge is still limited to vehicles under 18 tonnes, and a speed limit of 20 miles per hour applies until a final inspection in June.

title: Red lentil soup
text:
Red lentil soup (serves four). Rinse 250 grams of red lentils until the water runs clear. Soften one chopped onion and two cloves of garlic in two tablespoons of olive oil for five minutes, then stir in a teaspoon of cumin and half a teaspoon of turmeric.

Add the lentils, one litre of vegetable stock and a diced carrot. Simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils collapse. Blend half of the soup, return it to the pot, and finish with the juice of one lemon and a pinch of salt.

The soup keeps for four days in the fridge and freezes well for up to three months.

title: Resetting the office router
text:
How to reset the office router. First, note down the current settings: the network name, the admin address 192.168.4.1, and the DHCP range 192.168.4.20 to 192.168.4.200.

Hold the recessed reset button for 15 seconds with a paperclip until the power light blinks amber. Wait about two minutes for the router to restart. Log in at the admin address with the default account printed on the label, then immediately change the administrator password.

Restore the saved network name and enable WPA3 encryption. Finally, update the firmware to version 2.8 before reconnecting the printers.

title: Tidewater 3.0 release notes
text:
Tidewater 3.0 was released on 9 June 2025. The headline change is a rewritten scheduler that cuts average job latency by 40 percent in our benchmarks. Python 3.9 is no longer supported; the minimum version is now 3.11.

New features include a plugin API, a command line flag --dry-run for every subcommand, and experimental support for PostgreSQL 16. The configuration file moved from tidewater.ini to tidewater.toml, and a migration tool converts old files automatically.

Fixed: a memory leak in the log writer (issue 1187) and a crash when two workers claimed the same job (issue 1203). Deprecated: the old REST endpoint /v1/jobs, which will be removed in 4.0.

title: Re: Conference venue
text:
Hi Sam,

Thanks for sending the venue shortlist. I visited the Lakeside Hall on Thursday. It seats 220 people, which fits our expected 180 attendees, and the hire fee is 2,800 euros per day including projector and microphones. Catering is extra at 24 euros per head.

The Old Mill is cheaper at 1,900 euros per day, but it only seats 120, so I would rule it out. The Lakeside Hall has step-free access and a car park for 60 vehicles, and the manager, Ines Valdez, can hold the date of 17 October until the end of this month without a deposit.

Can you confirm the budget by Friday so I can book?

Best,
Omar

title: Lecture notes: photosynthesis
text:
Lecture 6: photosynthesis. Plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. The overall reaction consumes six molecules of carbon dioxide and six of water to produce one molecule of glucose and six of oxygen.

The light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes and produce ATP and NADPH. The Calvin cycle, also called the light-independent reactions, takes place in the stroma and uses that ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide.

Chlorophyll a absorbs mostly red and blue light, and reflects green, which is why leaves look green. The enzyme RuBisCO catalyses the first major step of carbon fixation and is considered the most abundant protein on Earth.

title: Trip report: Lisbon workshop
text:
Trip report: Lisbon data workshop, 3 to 5 November. I travelled by train and flight, arriving on the evening of 2 November. The workshop had about 90 participants from 14 countries.

Three takeaways. First, the keynote by Dr. Amara Nwosu argued that data quality checks should run at ingestion, not afterwards. Second, two teams reported that switching from nightly to hourly batches reduced stale-report complaints by half. Third, the vendor showcase confirmed that open table formats are now supported by every major warehouse.

Expenses came to 1,150 euros: 540 for flights, 420 for the hotel and 190 for meals. I recommend we send two people next year and submit a talk about our schema checks.

title: Remote work policy update
text:
Memo: remote work policy update, effective 1 July 2025. All employees may work remotely up to three days per week, with core in-office days on Tuesday and Wednesday. Managers can approve exceptions of up to four weeks per year for work abroad, provided the country is on the approved list maintained by HR.

Equipment: the company reimburses up to 300 euros once every three years for a desk chair or monitor. Internet costs are not reimbursed. Employees must use the company VPN when handling customer data.

Questions go to the people team at people@example.org. This policy replaces the version dated 15 January 2023.

title: Library FAQ
text:
Library FAQ. How many books can I borrow? Adult members may borrow up to 12 items at a time for 21 days; children may borrow 8 items for 14 days. Can I renew? Items can be renewed twice online unless another member has reserved them.

What are the late fees? Fees are 20 cents per day per item, capped at 6 euros per item. Children under 12 are never charged. How do I join? Bring a photo ID and proof of address to any branch; membership is free for residents of the district.

The central branch opens Monday to Saturday from 9:00 to 19:00 and closes on public holidays.

title: Review: Sonar Q5 headphones
text:
Review: Sonar Q5 wireless headphones. After two weeks of daily use the Q5 mostly impresses. Battery life is the standout: I measured 38 hours with noise cancelling on, close to the 40 claimed by the maker. The price is 179 euros, which undercuts the Bose-style competition by about 100.

Sound is balanced with a slightly warm bass. Noise cancelling handles train rumble well but struggles with voices in an open office. The ear cushions get warm after about ninety minutes. Bluetooth 5.3 connected to my phone and laptop at the same time without trouble, but the companion app is clumsy and crashed twice.

Verdict: recommended at this price, 4 out of 5.

title: Incident report: 7 May outage
text:
Incident report: checkout outage on 7 May 2025. Between 14:12 and 15:03 UTC customers could not complete purchases; 3,420 orders failed and were retried automatically, and about 310 never completed.

Root cause: a database migration added an index on the orders table without the concurrent option, which locked the table for 51 minutes. The change had passed review but was not tested against production-sized data. The on-call engineer, Kwame Asante, paged the database team at 14:20 and cancelled the migration at 15:01.

Actions: require concurrent index creation in the migration checklist (owner: Lena, due 23 May); add a staging dataset with 50 million rows (owner: Kwame, due 6 June); add an alert for lock waits longer than 30 seconds.
